references.text: Balaam uses the same introductory formula 'נְאֻם בִּלְעָם בְּנוֹ בְעֹר' (oracle of Balaam, son of Beor) and describes himself as 'שְׁתֻם הָעָיִן' (the man with the open eye) earlier in the same prophecy.
Balaam 'took up his oracle' (וַיִּשָּׂא מְשָׁלוֹ) - this same phrasing is used to introduce Balaam's prophetic oracles.
Balaam 'took up his oracle and said' (וַיִּשָּׂא מְשָׁלוֹ וַיֹּאמַר) - an identical introductory formula as in 24:15.
Balaam is identified as 'son of Beor' (בְּנוֹ בְעֹר), the same genealogical identification used in 24:15.
Peter mentions Balaam, son of Bosor (Βαλαὰμ τοῦ Βοσόρ), as a false prophet and links him to prophetic speech.
John refers to the teaching of Balaam (τὴν διδαχὴν Βαλαάμ) in Revelation, pointing to his prophetic role.
